title: pause LANE stops the lane before its next round, not only at the top of its loop
description: Seen 2026-09-21 01:36-01:48 UTC: bead-supervisor pause gpu, pause cpu, pause claude (all three pause.* flags in the state dir until 02:07); the journal shows only 'claude lane paused; starting nothing until resume'. title: the pipeline's merge step on a protected repo: ask GitHub to auto-merge on green instead of merging inside the build that is the required check
description:
scripts/ci-merge.sh (the last step of a PR build, .buildkite/pipeline.yml) squash-merges the PR with PUT /repos/OWNER/REPO/pulls/N/merge. On bead-loop that can never succeed: main's branch protection requires the status check `buildkite/bead-loop`, and that check *is* the build the step runs in, so GitHub answers `405: Required status check "buildkite/bead-loop" is pending` (build #19 on PR #39, 2026-09-20), the step exits 1, and the failure turns the required check red — a green build reported as a failed one. Every bead-loop PR so far was merged by hand for this reason; on inquire-platform the same script works only because that repo is private with no branch protection. `enforce_admins` is on, so there is no bypass. The `automerge` label was created on bead-loop and deleted again the same day: with it, the loop's own PRs here would go red on this step and be sent back as "CI red".

Fix, in scripts/ci-merge.sh: when the PUT answers 405 and the message names a pending required status check, do not fail — enable GitHub's auto-merge on the PR instead (public repos have it), and exit 0 saying so. GraphQL: first `query { repository(owner:, name:) { pullRequest(number:) { id } } }` for the node id, then `mutation { enablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId:, mergeMethod: SQUASH, expectedHeadOid: SHA}) { pullRequest { autoMergeRequest { enabledAt } } } }` — the same token (an installation token with pull_requests: write may call GraphQL). GitHub then merges the moment this build's status turns green, which is the outcome the label asked for; if auto-merge is already enabled, treat that as done. Any other 405 (conflicts) stays a failure as today. Then, since the label is the opt-in, create the `automerge` label on bead-loop again (`gh label create automerge`) — the loop labels every PR it opens under merge = "pipeline" and holds the bead when it cannot. The merge watcher (src/merge.rs, "pipeline") already closes the bead once the PR is MERGED. README: the Checks and the pipeline section says the step merges; say when it asks GitHub to instead. inquire-platform's scripts/ci-merge.mjs is the same script in node and should get the same branch, in its own PR there.

Proof is a shell test, since the pipeline cannot run here: a fake `curl` on PATH (test/bin has the pattern) that answers the PUT with 405 and that message, then answers the two GraphQL calls; the script exits 0 and its output says auto-merge was enabled with the expected head; a 405 with another message still exits 1.
acceptance_criteria: On a PR build of bead-loop with the automerge label, the :github: automerge step exits 0 and the PR merges once the build's status is green (seen on the first labelled PR after this lands). A test under test/ (a case in run.sh or a new script the gate runs) drives scripts/ci-merge.sh with a stub curl: 405 "Required status check ... is pending" → the GraphQL enablePullRequestAutoMerge call is made with the build's sha and the script exits 0; 405 with any other message → exit 1; 200 → "merged" as today. shellcheck passes; the whole gate in .bead-loop.toml passes.

title: a repeated hold re-arms its backoff: the same reason again touches held/ID, so a bead the server keeps refusing is retried every 5 min, not every pass
description:
On 2026-09-20 between 16:00 and 17:40 UTC the Claude lane ran inq-8gg.8 781 times — one `claude -p` every ~7 s, each answered with "You've hit your session limit", each logged as a hold "no failure charged" (the scoreboard counts them as 800 empty rounds in the week; ~/.local/state/bead-loop/inquire-platform/logs/inq-8gg.8.20260920T16*.worker.jsonl are the empty files, their .err the message).

The cause is in src/state.rs `Repo::hold`: when the reason is the same as the one already in held/ID it returns false *without writing the file*, so the file's mtime — which `round::hold_expired` (src/round.rs) reads through `held_since` as the hold's age — stays at the first hold. Once that is BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF (300 s) old, every later hold with the same reason is expired the moment it is placed; `round::hold` then rings the bell (`repo.wake()`), the lane looks again at once, picks the same bead, runs the harness, gets the same refusal, holds again — a tight loop rung by its own bell. The second hold was meant to be silent (no second note on the bead, no second log line), not free of backoff.

Fix: in `Repo::hold`, when the reason is unchanged, touch the file (crate::util::touch, or rewrite it) before returning false, so the backoff clock restarts from the latest hold. Keep the return value as it is: the caller's note and log line still happen once per reason. The unit test `hold_is_said_once_per_reason` in src/state.rs gains the mtime check; `test/run.sh` `case_harness_down_is_held` (or a new case) proves the wiring: with BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF=2 and the harness stub answering nothing, a `--once tick` right after the second hold does not run the worker again, and one two seconds later does.

Related, not this bead: bl-btp (exponential backoff and park after a day) and bl-ycs (a provider down holds the lane, not each bead) build on this; this one only makes the existing 5 min backoff hold true on the second and every later hold.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test state::tests::hold_is_said_once_per_reason passes with an added assertion that a second `hold` with the same reason leaves `held_since` no older than the moment of that second hold (set the file's mtime back first, e.g. with libc::utimensat as review_queue_is_fewest_failures_then_oldest does, and check it moved forward). test/run.sh has a case where, with BEAD_LOOP_HOLD_BACKOFF=2 and a harness that exits with no output, two ticks in a row make one worker call each (the hold, then the retry after the backoff) and a third tick inside the two seconds makes none — the stub's $TEST_CTRL/calls counts them. title: utility: the resident 4B on ac-box takes the loop's cheap calls -- a pre-check before the review, a post-mortem on a failed round
description:
WHY. Since 20 Sep 2026 (homelab-8r5) ac-box serves `utility`: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 Q8, resident beside coder, reviewer and embed, 8 threads, 16k ctx, ~9-12 tok/s -- a title in 1-4 s, 200 tokens in ~22 s, and it evicts nothing. Nothing in the loop calls it: bead-loop sets its own session titles, so opencode's small_model never fires, and the model's other job (pre-checks) is a design this epic supplies. The reviewer (gpt-oss-120b) costs 70-300 s per call and one slot on the cpu lane; on 21 Sep, 9 of 11 rounds died at the gate and the two that reached review were mechanically deficient in ways a 4B can see. The cheap model belongs where a judgment call is small and the round is otherwise going to spend the expensive one.

WHERE IT FITS. Two seams, both inline in the round that is already running -- NOT a lane round (a lane takes rounds by model glob, and `acbox/utility` would queue a gpu bead's pre-check behind the cpu lane; utility is resident and one-slot, so a synchronous call from any lane is safe, and two at once queue for seconds inside llama-server).

  worker round -> settle -> gate (+ one fix round) -> [PRE-CHECK: utility] -> review queue -> reviewer -> PR
                                                          |
                                  SEND BACK: one failure, the block to the worker, same as a REJECT
  send_back(note carrying only a tail) -> [POST-MORTEM: utility] -> the note also says what the worker tried and where it stopped

1. PRE-CHECK (src/round.rs dev_one, between the gate passing and write_file(review_path)): the bead, the DONE line, the diffstat and the diff (cut to 24000 bytes: the model's context is 16k tokens) go to agent `bead-prechecker` on `precheck_model`. It judges three mechanical things and nothing else: the DONE line quotes a command and its real output, not a claim; the diff touches only files the DESCRIPTION names; nothing was added the bead did not ask for (dependency, flag, variable, route). `PASS: <what it checked>` -> the review queue as today. `SEND BACK: <one line>` + the `For the worker:` block -> send_back: ONE FAILURE, like a REJECT, because a send-back is a send-back -- the difference is 20 s instead of 5 min of the reviewer, and the reviewer's slot stays free. Anything else (server error, empty, unparsed, timeout 180 s) -> logged and the round goes on to review: the pre-check never blocks and never holds; the loop without a utility model is the loop today.

2. POST-MORTEM (src/round.rs, the three send_back notes that carry only a tail: "worker made no commit. Last words:", "worker exited N", "gate failed twice"): one call with the worker log's assistant text (last 8000 bytes) and the gate tail, answering in <= 5 lines what the worker tried, where it stopped, and the first thing the next round should do. Appended to the note under "Post-mortem (MODEL):" -- the note is the work order the next worker reads and the history the briefer summarises, and today it is three lines of tail.

CONFIG. One key, global or per repo, empty by default: `precheck_model = "acbox/utility"` (used by both seams; a second key is not warranted until the two want different models). The opencode provider already has `acbox/utility` (context 16384, tool_call true); the live ~/.config/bead-loop/config.toml is hand-edited on this box (install.sh writes it only when absent) -- that is the owner's step, last.

DEPLOY, END TO END. A child merges -> the pipeline cuts release main-<sha> -> bead-loop-deploy.timer's scripts/deploy.sh installs the binary, re-links agents/*.md (install.sh), restarts opencode-web.service because agents/ changed, and the running loop re-execs at its next idle moment. So a new agent file reaches ~/.config/opencode/agents/ by the same merge that ships the code that calls it; nothing is placed by hand except the config key.

DOGFOOD. The children carry delegate:local, so the loop works them with its own stages; once the last one is deployed and the key is set, the loop's own rounds on this repo are pre-checked. Proof, in order: (a) `journalctl --user -u bead-supervisor | grep 'precheck ('` shows PASS and SEND BACK lines on real rounds with durations under a minute; (b) a SEND BACK's bd note carries a For the worker block and the next round fixes it without a reviewer call; (c) `bead-supervisor stats` prints the pre-check line (child 4); (d) after ~30 rounds, the share of rounds the reviewer sends back for mechanical reasons (files not named, DONE without evidence) has fallen -- read the review notes. If (d) does not move, the pre-check is not earning its 20 s and the key comes out; the code stays, off by default.

ORDER. .1 (key, agent, prompt, parser) -> .2 (wired into the round, test case, README) and .3 (post-mortem) in either order -> .4 (stats, config template) -> the owner sets the key and watches (a)-(d).

title: the loop rejoins the sessions it was on after its own restart
description: scripts/deploy.sh recycles the whole stack on every deploy — opencode-web.service too — so every deploy kills every model session in flight and the beads on the lanes start their rounds over (recover reopens them; see also the bead on failures charged during a stop). The sessions live in opencode-web.service, not in the supervisor: a supervisor restart need not lose them. Two parts. (1) deploy.sh restarts opencode-web.service only when the deployed commit changed agents/ or skills/ (git diff --quiet <deployed> <want> -- agents skills, with <deployed> from $DEPLOY/deployed; the first deploy restarts it), and bead-loop-ui.service only when bin/ or ui/ changed; the supervisor is restarted every time (the binary). (2) In src/lanes.rs recover: instead of aborting every session under wt/<id>, a lane thread whose bead has a running session (GET $attach/session/status for the worktree, as abort_sessions does) rejoins it — resumes waiting on that session for its final text as harness::run would, with the round's timeout counted from the session's start — so a bead mid-round on a deploy carries on where it was; a session that is not running is treated as today. The signals handler then stops aborting sessions on TERM and only removes markers and exits (a plain stop still aborts: 'bead-supervisor stop --abort', or a flag in the unit's ExecStop — decide in the bead and document it in README 'How the loop waits'). Files: scripts/deploy.sh, src/lanes.rs (recover), src/harness.rs (a rejoin: wait on an existing session id), src/signals.rs, test/run.sh (a case: worker mode hang with a stub server that reports a session, TERM, run again — the round completes without a second bead-worker call), README.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy that changes only src/ leaves opencode-web.service and bead-loop-ui.service running (their PIDs unchanged across the deploy); a supervisor restart mid-round ends with the same session's result, no second worker call, no failure charged; the whole gate is green.
